en: As recorded in the *Tathāgata in the Golden Coffin Entrusts the Sutra of Pure Adornment and Reverent Merit*, newly translated from the Western Hu Kingdom and included within the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*:
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying between the twin śāla trees in the city of Kuśinagara.
he was about to enter his golden coffin,
Sitting cross-legged upon the railing of the golden coffin,
his two eyes shed tears that emitted light and caused the earth to tremble;
the vast assembly of immeasurable bodhisattvas, along with the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, all gave rise to doubt.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, you now wish to universally address the great assembly to resolve their doubts;
I wonder if you will grant me leave to speak?"
World-Honored One, Tathāgata, you have always taught that nirvāṇa is eternal, blissful, and forever free from birth and death.
For what reason do you now sit upon this golden coffin and casket with tears streaming down, causing the assembly to doubt?
